sn36.1:2.1: The text is not explicit as to who speaks these verses. Nor, for that matter, does it say who spoke the prose; the context is elided, presumably because the editors thought it was obvious that it is the Buddha speaking. The same is true of the verses. Indeed, [iti52]() is otherwise identical to this discourse, except it indicates that the Buddha spoke the verses. Whether the verses were added later is a separate matter, but clearly the text presents them as the Buddha’s words.
sn36.1:3.4: By treating the feelings according to the four noble truths, the Buddha is implicitly situating all feelings as suffering.
